That's really clear, thank you — I can picture the problem now. Let me play back what I understand, so we're aligned before I build anything:

**The goal:** One personal, trustworthy collection for your links — so bookmarks stop being a place where things disappear and become something you actually use. Two things matter most:

- **Saving is nearly effortless** — you drop in a link, the app pulls in the useful details itself, and you can lightly adjust the title/description and add tags or a note if you want.
- **Finding it again is reliable, even months later** — through searching by anything you remember, browsing a topic by tag, and a separate "read later" space so unfinished reading stays out of the way of everything else.

Two quick checks to make sure I've got the emphasis right:

1. Is the heart of this really about **trusting that nothing gets lost and you can always find it again** — with effortless saving as the thing that makes you actually keep using it? Or is the effortless capture itself the main prize?

2. When you say "read later" — do you picture a bookmark **starting** in read-later and then graduating into your main collection once you've read it? Or is "read later" just a label/view you flip on and off, with everything living in one collection regardless?

And one thing you haven't mentioned yet: **where do you imagine using this** — mostly at your computer in a browser, on your phone, or both?
